findings.title: Detached capture survives a killed supervisor
findings.trigger: A supervisor killed with SIGKILL releases its lock without reliably terminating its FFmpeg child. Synthetic segmented capture continued from three to five files after parent death.
findings.impact: Capture can continue beyond the visible controller; recovery may inspect archives still being written. The reproduction uses lavfi, not a microphone; actual fallback-session end-to-end capture was not run.
findings.recommendation: Give the child a verified parent-death lifetime and durable PID/start-identity ownership. Recovery must establish that every owned writer has stopped before validating/exporting archives. Prefer existing systemd cgroup supervision where available, with a tested fallback.
findings.validation: Kill a synthetic fallback parent; require child termination, no new segments and safe recovery. Cover startup races, PID reuse and normal graceful stop.

findings.title: Storage failures can bypass shutdown
findings.trigger: Metadata reads/writes occur before halt_capture and route cleanup inside finalization. An I/O exception can escape before teardown.
findings.impact: A full/unwritable filesystem can leave recording/routing resources running or unrecovered.
findings.recommendation: Place child termination, routing restoration and socket closure in independent finally blocks; make failure reporting best-effort after teardown.
findings.validation: Inject ENOSPC, failed fsync/rename and corrupt metadata at each finalization boundary. All cleanup attempts must occur and originals must remain.

findings.title: Failed unload forgets the owned audio module
findings.trigger: unload pops the module ID, swallows pactl failure and saves the empty ownership journal. A mocked failure reproduced the loss in memory and on disk.
findings.impact: An old loopback can remain active while replacements load and recovery no longer knows it.
findings.recommendation: Delete ownership only after successful unload or verified absence; retain failed historical IDs separately when replacing a labeled module.
findings.validation: Fail unload, create a replacement, then retry cleanup. Both owned IDs must stay tracked until verified gone; unrelated modules remain untouched.

findings.title: Automatic call transitions are dropped while busy
findings.trigger: worker returns when another start/stop action is running. A call-end debounce can fire during slow startup and be discarded permanently.
findings.impact: Opt-in automatic recording can continue after a short call ends, or miss the next call during finalization.
findings.recommendation: Keep latest desired call state and reconcile it after every operation. Preserve owned-session checks and explicit unknown-state behavior. Do not use an unbounded event queue.
findings.validation: Block mocked startup, deliver call end, release startup and require owned-session stop. Also deliver a new call during blocked stop and simulate bus loss.

findings.title: Suspend detection uses the wrong clock
findings.trigger: Linux monotonic time excludes suspended time, but it drives the suspend-gap detector, epoch offsets and final duration. Display elapsed time uses wall time.
findings.impact: Suspend can be omitted from the promised gap timeline; saved and displayed durations can disagree. FFmpeg offset consequences still need integration measurement.
findings.recommendation: Define one elapsed session timeline with CLOCK_BOOTTIME and detect suspend from boottime/monotonic delta differences. Keep wall timestamps only as presentation anchors.
findings.validation: Inject independently advancing clocks, verify gap/offset/duration agreement, then run an authorized real suspend acceptance test.

findings.title: Late Teams instances bypass ambiguity checks
findings.trigger: Starting without Teams playback leaves teams_pid unset; later routing matches every Teams PID without rechecking ambiguity.
findings.impact: Unrelated Teams profiles/calls can be mixed into one recording.
findings.recommendation: Persist an explicit selection policy; bind an initially unbound recording only to an unambiguous process. Surface ambiguity before moving any newly ambiguous streams.
findings.validation: Empty startup inventory followed by two different Teams PIDs; assert neither is silently routed. Cover explicit selection and process replacement.

findings.title: Recovery and processing can race on exports
findings.trigger: Recovery takes a global recording lock while processing takes a different session processing lock. Both can export the same session into identical temporary paths.
findings.impact: Concurrent recovery/preparation can corrupt or replace derivatives during use and leave inconsistent metadata.
findings.recommendation: Use one shared per-session audio-artifact lock for repair, export and preparation, with a documented lock order.
findings.validation: Synchronize two processes at export creation; one must wait/refuse. Verify final hashes, metadata and retained originals.

findings.title: A blocked export read has no deadline
findings.trigger: stdout.read can block before proc.wait(timeout=30) is reached.
findings.impact: Stop/finalization can hold the recording lock indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Use selectable streaming reads with an overall deadline and guaranteed child termination; reuse a shared bounded subprocess primitive.
findings.validation: A synthetic child emits a short block and holds stdout open. Require bounded interruption, released locks and preserved archives.

findings.title: Connected health does not verify the capture route
findings.trigger: Private sink and physical-device checks do not validate owned loopback existence/endpoints or same-name device recreation.
findings.impact: The GUI can show a connected microphone while its loopback is absent and the archive contains silence.
findings.recommendation: Track device/module incarnation and verify route endpoints. Expose physical presence, route health and capture progress separately.
findings.validation: Remove a loopback while keeping devices and sinks unchanged; require warning/gap/repair. Recreate a device with the same name and new identity.

findings.title: Health remains green when the supervisor snapshot is stale
findings.trigger: Status accepts a live PID and merges the last snapshot without recalculating its age; saved progress age freezes when the worker stalls.
findings.impact: A stalled worker can continue to appear healthy.
findings.recommendation: Compute snapshot age at read time and expose stale/unknown status after a documented threshold. Distinguish process existence from progress.
findings.validation: Advance a fake clock against a frozen snapshot and matching PID; require stale health in CLI and GUI.

findings.title: A native-audio refusal does not stop later submissions
findings.trigger: A schema-valid audio_received=false result becomes MeetingError, but only AIError breaks the loop. The local stub was called for both chunks after its first refusal.
findings.impact: The program continues unnecessary data submissions and quota use after capability failure, contrary to its documented stop policy. Existing consent was present; this is not a claim of upload without initial consent.
findings.recommendation: Introduce provider-neutral session-fatal/capability refusal categories. Stop subsequent calls, persist a blocked reason and retain unprocessed intervals. Keep specific size-limit splitting.
findings.validation: Three mocked chunks, first native-audio refusal: exactly one submission, incomplete coverage and durable diagnostics.

findings.title: Terminating Q&A/probe can leave the provider alive
findings.trigger: Only process translates SIGTERM into handled cancellation. Other hosted paths spawn a new provider session; default parent SIGTERM bypasses its cleanup. A harmless fake agy survived parent termination.
findings.impact: A hosted request may continue after the initiating application exits. No actual provider was contacted in this review.
findings.recommendation: Wrap every hosted entry point with shared cancellation handling and process-group teardown; restore signal handlers and mark attempts cancelled. Also handle supervisor hard-death lifetime.
findings.validation: Fake agy records PID then waits; terminate ask/probe parents and require no surviving child, released locks and interrupted attempt state.

findings.title: Historical Q&A links point into a mutable transcript
findings.trigger: Answers link to sequential IDs in the overwritten shared transcript. A local stub answer stayed unchanged while its cited anchor was replaced by contradictory synthetic dialogue.
findings.impact: Retained answers can appear supported by different evidence after correction or retranscription.
findings.recommendation: Save immutable transcript revisions or minimal evidence snapshots per question, and qualify links with revision identity. Reuse existing source hashes; do not add a database for this.
findings.validation: Ask, correct/reorder/delete source segments, then open historical evidence. It must still show the originally cited text and revision.

findings.title: Model text is rendered as active Markdown
findings.trigger: Transcript and notes preserve model-authored images/links/HTML. Synthetic remote-image markup survived both renderers; no viewer was opened.
findings.impact: Forged links can misrepresent evidence. Remote-resource-capable viewers may make network requests when opened; actual fetching is viewer-dependent and was not tested.
findings.recommendation: Centralize literal text escaping, keep app-generated evidence links separate and retain exact raw transcript text in JSON. Support code through controlled rendering.
findings.validation: Images, HTML, headings, forged evidence links and table escapes must render literally; generated local evidence links remain usable.

findings.title: A single large segment bypasses notes request bounds
findings.trigger: The splitter checks size only for a nonempty block and counts characters. A 200000-character Devanagari segment reached a local stub as a 601032-byte prompt.
findings.impact: Large requests can exceed provider limits or consume unintended quota; existing resumable behavior does not impose a bound on every request.
findings.recommendation: Check complete serialized UTF-8 request size before each call, including instructions. Reject oversized single segments before submission or split them into explicitly linked spans.
findings.validation: Single oversize segment, many ordinary segments and multibyte text; no over-budget prompt may reach the adapter.

findings.title: Cached output has no independent accepted-output digest
findings.trigger: Input fingerprints do not detect a schema-valid cached transcript/notes edit that preserves its fingerprint.
findings.impact: Accidental or same-user cached-output changes can silently alter provenance. This is not a remote compromise or protection against an attacker able to rewrite every baseline.
findings.recommendation: Separate accepted output revisions/digests from disposable input-keyed caches. Explicit imports create an auditable new revision. Align the baseline promise in SECURITY.md with the implemented scope.
findings.validation: Modify valid cached text without changing input fingerprint; require rejection/invalidation. Explicit correction imports remain supported.

findings.title: npm wrapper upgrades silently run the old runtime
findings.trigger: Version matching occurs during setup only; ordinary launch uses any existing shared npm-runtime.
findings.impact: A future wrapper B can launch native A without an actionable compatibility warning. Only version0.1.0 is currently declared; no real upgrade was executed.
findings.recommendation: Persist/check native version and runtime installation identity before launch; require explicit setup on mismatch. Define the override executable compatibility policy too.
findings.validation: Newer staged wrapper plus older synthetic native runtime: recording commands must fail with explicit setup guidance. Same-version reinstall remains valid.

findings.title: Source GUI installation lacks its GTK minimum guard
findings.trigger: Native packages require GTK>=4.10, but source/wheel startup and doctor accept any GTK4. AlertDialog exists only since4.10.
findings.impact: GTK4.8 source installations fail at required confirmation instead of reporting an actionable dependency error.
findings.recommendation: Check GTK>=4.10 before window construction and state it consistently in source installation/contributor docs.
findings.validation: Mock4.8: dependency exit3 before constructing window; accept4.10. Native dependency metadata remains versioned.

findings.title: Folder stays disabled after the first GUI session
findings.trigger: Empty history disables all output buttons; subsequent state updates restore notes/transcript only.
findings.impact: A first-session user cannot open its folder without reopening the application.
findings.recommendation: Set every output button sensitivity from current state on every update.
findings.validation: Empty→recording→recorded without recreating the window; Folder becomes enabled.

findings.title: Service and shortcut examples assume a source launcher
findings.trigger: Examples use ~/.local/bin/shruta, whereas native packages install /usr/bin/shruta.
findings.impact: Following these examples after native installation can produce a failed service or inactive shortcut.
findings.recommendation: Document channel-specific executable paths or generate an explicitly installed unit from a resolved owned executable. Avoid shadow launchers.
findings.validation: Check source/native/npm unit and shortcut commands, including paths containing spaces.

findings.title: Arch metadata regression tests are omitted from normal CI
findings.trigger: Default testpaths contains tests only. The two Arch generator tests ran only when explicitly named.
findings.impact: Traversal and source-pinning regressions can pass ordinary CI.
findings.recommendation: Move the suite under tests or include its path explicitly in every required test job. Prefer one collection convention.
findings.validation: pytest --collect-only must include both Arch metadata cases; unsafe archive fixtures must still be rejected.

findings.title: The ten-minute deadline is per attempt
findings.trigger: Each of three attempts gets the full configured600seconds.
findings.impact: A chunk may take roughly30minutes plus cleanup/backoff, not one ten-minute total deadline.
findings.recommendation: State per-attempt and total bounds explicitly, or implement one shared overall deadline.
findings.validation: A fake clock verifies retry allocation and total elapsed budget.
